morning coffee with milk, a window
overlooking a cherry tree.

not a story, but a stanza—

I noticed the shadow of my hand
on the wall—how it moved
like a separate creature,
obeying its own laws.
I tried to make it stop,
but it continued, indifferent,
reminding me that I am not the master
of even this small darkness.
For the first time in my life,
I questioned whether I am the dreamer
or the dream.
The stars, once scattered ornaments,
now seemed like pinpricks in a veil,
and I wondered what lay beyond.
I looked at my reflection in a pond
and saw not a face but a surface,
rippling with the weight of questions.
Who is this I that thinks it knows 'I'?
For the first time in my life,
I was afraid of the answer.
Perhaps there is no self—
just a river of moments,
and this body a temporary bank.
I sat on the grass and watched the clouds
unmake themselves.
For the first time in my life,
I was not sad or happy—
just present, a witness
in a universe of witnesses,
all of us asking, silently,
what it means to be here, now.
